messages.author: 4bfae3793264e847
messages.subject: sparse data
parts:
Hi everybody,

I try to estimate pop.densities for the same species in several independent sites (live trapping of small mammals). On several sites the capture succes was extremely low (e.g. 2 individuals and no recaptures, 8 individuals 2 recaptures, etc.). I am convinced though that the low capture numbers reflect the low pop.size/pop.density in the respective sites and are not artefacts of our trapping procedures.
Is there a threshold up to which it does not make sense to use secr to estimate densities?
I tried to fit several models to the datasets and in some cases the estimates seem to be "reasonable". In most cases however the density estimates from the best fitting models definitely do not make sense and the SEs are also out of control... (see example below). I did try several mask settings, different starting values for D, g0 and sigma, but the values did still not seem to be meaningful.

Thanks for any help!

Cheers,
Julian

secrAS41 <- secr.fit (psemiCH.AS4, model = g0~1, mask = AS4.mask, CL = FALSE,
    start = list(D=1, g0=0.1, sigma=17), method = "BFGS")
secrAS42 <- secr.fit (psemiCH.AS4, model = g0~b , mask = AS4.mask, CL = FALSE,
    start = list(D=1, g0=0.1, sigma=17), method = "BFGS")
secrAS43 <- secr.fit (psemiCH.AS4, model = list(g0~b, sigma~b), mask = AS4.mask, CL = FALSE,
    start = list(D=1, g0=0.1, sigma=17), method = "BFGS")
secrAS44 <- secr.fit (psemiCH.AS4, model = list(g0~b, sigma~b), mask = AS4.mask, CL = FALSE,
    start = list(D=1, g0=0.1, sigma=17), method = "BFGS")
secrAS45 <- secr.fit (psemiCH.AS4, model = g0~b+T, mask = AS4.mask, CL = FALSE,
    start = list(D=1, g0=0.1, sigma=17), method = "BFGS")

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: sparse data
parts:
Julian
There's no simple threshold, but you really cannot expect sensible results with such data (probably no capture-recapture method can be expected to work well without at least tens of recaptures). Also, there are two limitations on precision: your ability to estimate the detection parameters (e.g., g0 and sigma) and the Poisson or binomial uncertainty associated with observing only a small integer number of individuals. Uncertainty in the detection parameters can be 'fixed' by pooling information across, e.g., trapping grids, to achieve enough recaptures etc. However, imprecision due to the other component is inescapable.
Murray

messages.author: b1d2e118c1689e57
messages.subject: RE: sparse data
parts:
Hi Julian,

 

Murray is correct. My personal experience using SECR on small mammals is it works extremely well (in so far as precision) on even quite sparse data. i.e. low density and recaptures. Where alternative non-sparse data are available to pool, e.g. a session somewhere else (perhaps another study) with high recaptures where you can defendably assume the sigma from that session is identical (for the sake of analysing your data), I have had good luck estimating reasonably precise density, even if density itself is low (i.e. uncertainty in a low g0).

 

James

James may tout the wondrous properties of SECR (silk purses from sow's ears etc.) but I feel the need to be more cautious! Following James's line, in the extreme one can just fix sigma at an externally-derived value (...fixed=list(sigma=xx)...) and declare that as an assumption.
Murray
